[Q1.] What is a "black hole"?
A black hole (BH) is an object with such strong gravity that nothing, not even light can escape from it. The gravitational force of BHs comes mainly from their mass and compactness; they have very high density because all matter in them has been compressed into small space by its own weight. A typical example would be our Sun if we could compress it to 10 km radius or less: then no one on Earth will ever see sunlight again!
